title: Rademacher is the sharp negative-kurtosis endpoint for weak symmetric channels

extremal_law.moment_floor: For every centered unit-variance X, E[X^4]>=(E[X^2])^2=1, hence kappa_4(X)>=-2.
extremal_law.equality_case: Equality holds iff X^2=1 almost surely; centering then forces the symmetric Rademacher law.
extremal_law.weak_gap: Writing u=-kappa_4(X) in [0,2], a block with limiting score weight tau and fourth-mass weight ell has local gap (u^2 tau/24)t^4-g u ell t^2+O_X(t^5).
extremal_law.effective_coordinate: With q=u t^2, the universal quadratic surrogate is (tau/24)q^2-g ell q, minimized at q_*=12g ell/tau with value -6g^2 ell^2/tau when the weak-channel range contains q_*.
extremal_law.rademacher_role: At fixed small t, Rademacher uniquely maximizes the reachable negative fourth-cumulant magnitude u t^2; it realizes u=2 and K1681's Fisher coefficient 2/3.
extremal_law.scope_guard: This is sharp fourth-moment and weak-channel leading-order extremality only. Higher Hermite terms can affect finite-t optimization, so no exact global Fisher-defect optimality is claimed.
